review_candidates.title: Events & Partner Marketing Lead
review_candidates.location: Copenhagen Municipality, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
review_candidates.description: About Us You know that rental bike you unlocked with your phone this morning? Or the tracker on your dog's collar that tells you he's two streets away, again? Neither of those works without a network connection. Onomondo is the layer that makes sure the data actually gets through. We're the infrastructure behind the Internet of Things (IoT). Companies building connected products come to us for the connectivity that keeps their devices online, anywhere in the world, and for the platform where they manage, monitor, and troubleshoot it themselves. Where we sit We're somewhere between SaaS and telecom. We sell software, so we move fast, ship often, and care about the user experience. But we also operate inside telecommunications: which is more complex and technical than most software. Our customers are engineers, they ask hard questions and the relationship starts rather than ends at purchase. That mix also makes us sticky. Most SaaS tools are nice to have. If our connectivity stops, our customers' products stop. That means our business grows as our customers and the industry grows. We've been growing fast and we don't plan to slow down, which is exactly why we need this role. Why this role exists Behind every connected product, whether it’s a tracker on a shipping container, a meter in a basement or a sensor on a wind turbine, is a team that figured out how to make software work in the physical world. They’re engineers and product leaders who want to see their product running for real, and meet people who have already solved the problem they’re stuck on. That’s why the decisions that matter here get made in a room, not an inbox. An engineer picks a connectivity provider after hearing a customer describe what broke at 2 a.m. A partner introduces us on their own stage. A buyer makes up their mind after a hallway conversation at a conference. We want to build and own those rooms. Today we run a big in-person summit, Made for IoT, plus online summits and webinars for the industries we care about, and we go to a long list of conferences every year, often next to our partners. A lot of our reach also comes through our partners’ events, launches and channels. Most of it has been planned project by project, and we want to plan it on purpose. This role is built to do that. You’ll be the project leader who owns the summits, decide where we show up and why, and look after the partner side: joint events and launches, the co-marketing budget and funding, and the partner hub. You’ll report to our Head of Growth Marketing. What you'll do Own Made for IoT, our in-person summit, from the agenda to the follow-up: format, speakers, promotion, logistics, the day itself and what happens after. Run our online summits. Shape the program, find the speakers, get the team excited and turn attendees into real conversations. Own our conference strategy. We have the 2027 list, but not yet what we want out of each event. You’ll decide how we show up and give every event a goal, a budget and a plan for the follow-up. Run co-marketing with partners, such as joint events and launches, and line up our calendar with the events our key partners host or join. Manage the co-marketing and event budget. Split it across partners and initiatives, secure funding from partners and make sure everyone delivers what we agreed. Own the partner surface: the partner hub, asset kit, joint decks and accurate listings on both sides. Own event reporting. Work with our Growth Operations Specialist to track registrations, attendance, meetings, pipeline and cost per outcome. Turn events into opportunities. Work with Sales, Customer Success and Marketing so every conference leads to real conversations, not just a list of badge scans. What we're looking for An events and partner marketer with a commercial head. Someone who can run a room full of people, and also ask whether the room was worth the money. Crucially, someone who can both plan and execute. A strong project leader who leads without a team. You keep many moving parts on track at once, and you don’t need someone to chase you. You’ll have no direct reports, so you get things done by bringing people with you, including partners, speakers, and colleagues in Sales, Customer Success and Marketing. A people person who loves events. You spend a lot of time talking to strangers and come away energised rather than drained. Ideally you already take part in community events on your own time. Commercial judgement. You can look at a conference or partner list and tell us which matter, and you’re comfortable saying no to the rest. You know the difference between a full room and a useful one. Around 3-5 years in B2B marketing, ideally in tech, SaaS or telecom. You’ve run events end to end and worked with partners on joint campaigns. A good writer and communicator, who can talk to an engineer in the audience and a CEO on the stage, and write the copy for agendas and slides. Measurement driven. You track what each campaign brings in, and you document and report so an event you run can be repeated and scaled. Curious about how things work. You don’t need to know what a SIM does today, but you should want to find out. Fluent in written and spoken English. Another language is a plus, but not a must. Life at Onomondo The things we build have global reach. The way we build them is personal. We're a team of engineers, operators, and commercial minds in Copenhagen who debate passionately about technical or GTM approaches and then go for a run together. Or padel. Or a beer. Or a boardgame night. People here stay curious, speak up when something feels off, and bring energy whether it's a product launch sprint or a Friday bar. You’ll get real ownership of your work, a team that invests in your growth, and a seat in an industry that keeps moving. On top of that: extra vacation days, full health insurance, a cooked-on-site lunch every day, an in-office gym with HIIT and yoga during work hours, and quarterly Friday bars. Applying Your application doesn't need to be polished. What we'd like to hear about is the events you've run before: summits, conferences, co-marketing campaigns, customer events, partner events, anything in that family. Tell us what you ran, what you were trying to achieve, and what happened. Our hiring process We care deeply about creating a fair and inclusive process. That means: We don’t need your picture We select candidates based on skills and relevant work experience for the role. What you can expect: Screening call with Madalina, our Head of People (Online, 30 minutes) Skill-based interview with Emelie, our Head of Growth Marketing (In-Person, 1 hour) Case-based interview with Emelie and Connor (Head of Brand Communications). Culture meet with a co-founder (the Grandparent interview round) (In-Person, 30 minutes) Our partner, Veremark, will also conduct a criminal record and right to work check. Note - We review and interview candidates continually, and therefore encourage you to apply at your earliest convenience.
